clue.text: Finish hosting mass dance

indicators.note: a host takes a guest in, so one word is put around the other

blocks.note: to finish is to stop
M is the physics symbol for mass

explanation.surface: A crowd brings an event to a close with one big dance.
explanation.walkthrough: STOP takes M inside it, giving STOMP.
explanation.definitionFit: A stomp is a lively dance with heavy, stamping steps, originally in jazz music.

clue.text: Increasingly guaranteed to suppress tear in cessation of hostilities?

indicators.note: suppressing something holds it down inside, so one word is clamped within another

blocks.note: more certain, the comparative of sure
to rend is to tear apart

explanation.surface: A truce seems ever more certain as someone holds back their tears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tear' tempts as weeping; it means rip. 'Increasingly guaranteed' is a comparative adjective. The question mark flags that giving in is one way, not the only way, hostilities stop.
explanation.definitionFit: Giving up to an enemy ends the fighting, so yielding is a way warfare comes to a stop.

clue.text: Antelope pen erected, supplied with electric current

indicators.note: in a down clue, something set upright reads from bottom to top

blocks.note: a Biro is a ballpoint pen, the British trade name
I is the physics symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: An enclosure for antelopes is put up and wired with an electric fence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pen' looks like an animal enclosure, matching the antelope, but it is a writing pen. A Biro is the everyday British word for a ballpoint.
explanation.definitionFit: The oribi is a small, slender African antelope of the grasslands, one species of that family.

clue.text: Officer in photo with old wind instrument

indicators.note: being in something means sitting inside it, so one piece goes within the rest

blocks.note: pic is a short informal word for a photo
Col is the abbreviation for colonel
O is a standard abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: An army officer poses for a photograph holding an antique flute.
explanation.walkthrough: The officer is a colonel, abbreviated as it appears in military ranks, and he stands inside the photo with the old marker tacked on.
explanation.definitionFit: A piccolo is a small flute pitched an octave higher, and flutes belong to the woodwind family.

clue.text: Ancient President continues to mock, interrupted by a couple of fellows

indicators.note: an interruption breaks into the middle of something, so one piece cuts inside another

blocks.note: to jeer on is to keep on mocking
F is the abbreviation for fellow, so two of them

explanation.surface: An elderly president keeps being heckled, though a couple of men cut in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Continues to mock' is a phrasal verb, jeering on. 'Ancient' is a loose way of saying he was president long ago.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Jefferson was the third US President, serving from 1801, so he belongs to the distant past.

clue.text: Not a real Pope - just one acting nobly at the outset

indicators.note: the outset is the start, so only the opening letter of each word counts

blocks.note: the initials of these four words

explanation.surface: A fake pontiff is unmasked as merely a performer playing a noble part.
explanation.walkthrough: Pope Joan is the legendary woman said to have reigned as pope in disguise in the Middle Ages; historians treat her as a myth.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary female pontiff never actually existed, so the tale describes a fictional rather than historical holder of the office.

clue.text: Concern about one shabby economic period

indicators.note: about here means around, so one word is wrapped round the others

blocks.note: a concern is a worry or fear
the Roman numeral one
scaly is British slang for shabby or mean

explanation.surface: Worry over one hard-up, shabby stretch of the economy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shabby' is not an anagram signal here; scaly is an old British slang word meaning shabby or stingy.
explanation.definitionFit: A financial year is the twelve-month accounting term used for budgets and tax, so it is a span of time in economics.

clue.text: Regret picking up half the letters for nuclear organisation

indicators.note: in a down clue, picking something up lifts it, so it reads from bottom to top

blocks.note: to rue is to regret
A to M is the first half of the alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone sorry for having opened only half the mail from an atomic agency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half the letters' reads as post; it means the alphabet from A TO M. Euratom is the European Atomic Energy Community.
explanation.definitionFit: Euratom is the European Atomic Energy Community, a body set up in 1957 to coordinate civilian atomic research and power.

clue.text: Confirm Elon M is whirling in empty space

indicators.note: something whirling is spun round, so its letters are thrown into a new order
an empty word has lost its contents, leaving just its outer letters
being in something means placed inside it, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: taken as written
the first and last letters

explanation.surface: A news item about a tech billionaire spinning about in a vacuum, fittingly for his rocket business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Elon M' points at a real person, but the letters are only fodder. The jumbled letters sit between the S and E of space.
explanation.definitionFit: To solemnise a marriage is to perform the formal ceremony that ratifies it, so it means to make official.

clue.text: Midday about time? It’s impracticable

indicators.note: about here means around, so one word encloses another

blocks.note: midday is twelve noon
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Someone asking to meet around noon is told the slot will not work.
explanation.walkthrough: Not on is informal British English for something unacceptable or unfeasible.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying a plan is not on is an idiom meaning it cannot be done or should not be allowed.

clue.text: Scoundrels seizing a popular firm making protective clothing

indicators.note: to seize is to grab hold, so one word takes the others into its grasp

blocks.note: rats are treacherous people
taken as written
in means fashionable or popular
Co is the abbreviation for company

explanation.surface: Crooks taking over a well-liked company that makes safety gear.
explanation.walkthrough: The scoundrels open after their first letter to take in the rest; Co is the standard abbreviation for company.
explanation.definitionFit: Waterproof coats shield the wearer from wet weather, so they are garments worn for shelter.

clue.text: Accept new tenant – show kindness, forgetting name

indicators.note: something forgotten is left out, so a letter is dropped

blocks.note: to relent is to soften and show mercy
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: A landlord takes in a new lodger, being kind enough not to ask their name.
explanation.walkthrough: RELENT loses its N.
explanation.definitionFit: To relet a property is to rent it out again, so the owner takes on a fresh occupant.

clue.text: Inventor backed team, never taking a different direction

indicators.note: something backed goes in reverse, so it reads right to left
heading the other way means the letters run in the opposite order

blocks.note: a side is a sports team
no as a flat refusal, never

explanation.surface: An inventor bets on a team, then changes course entirely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backed' looks like betting support for the team, but it is a direction signal; both halves are read right to left.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Edison was the American who devised the phonograph and a practical light bulb.

clue.text: Frankly, a German writer has penned a word in French after reflection

indicators.note: a reflection is a mirror image, so the letters read backwards
a pen is an enclosure, so one piece is shut inside another

blocks.note: taken as written
mot is French for word
Thomas Mann, German novelist

explanation.surface: To be candid, a German author slipped a French word into his text after some thought.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Has penned' suggests writing, apt for an author, but it means enclosing. The German writer is Thomas Mann, author of Death in Venice.
explanation.definitionFit: A man-to-man talk is open and honest, so the phrase used as an adverb means speaking candidly.

clue.text: Reserve litre during finishing off beer production, dismissing no good source of artwork

indicators.note: during means in the middle of, so one piece goes inside another
to dismiss is to send away, so letters are removed

blocks.note: ice is coldness or reserve of manner
L is the abbreviation for litre
beer is bottled as the last brewery step
NG is the abbreviation for no good

explanation.surface: A brewery keeps back some beer while bottling, discarding bad batches, with a nod to artwork on the labels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reserve' looks like a verb, to keep back, but it is a noun: coolness of manner. 'Source of artwork' is a playful way to name a painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Botticelli was the Florentine Renaissance painter of The Birth of Venus, so paintings come from him.

clue.text: Risky to accept dangerous order, creating difference of opinion

indicators.note: accepting something takes it in, so one word holds the others

blocks.note: dicy means risky
hot can mean dangerous, as in too hot to handle
OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: Obeying a dangerous command is a gamble that divides opinion.
explanation.walkthrough: DICY takes HOT and OM before its last letter. OM stands for the Order of Merit, an honour given by the British monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A dichotomy is a sharp division into two contrasting camps, so it can describe a split between views.

clue.text: Conservative head bracketing MP with a colleague

indicators.note: brackets go on both sides, so one word surrounds the others

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative
onion is British slang for the head, as in 'off your onion'
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Tory party leader teams up with an MP alongside a fellow member.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conservative head' looks like the party leader; it is C followed by a slang word for head. ONION is British slang for the head.
explanation.definitionFit: A companion is someone you work or travel alongside, a partner or associate, much like a coworker.

clue.text: Fate indicated by doctor having troubled air

indicators.note: something troubled is disturbed, so the letters are thrown out of order

blocks.note: MO is a Medical Officer
taken as written

explanation.surface: A doctor with a worried manner reveals someone's destiny.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Air' looks like a person's manner, matching a doctor's bedside demeanour, but it is just the three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Moira is the Greek word for one's allotted portion in life, personified as destiny, the Moirai being the Greek goddesses of it.

clue.text: Accepted French article about fruit is something powered by AI?

indicators.note: about here means around, so one word goes round another

blocks.note: A is an abbreviation for accepted, used on bills
un is the French for a
the tomato is botanically a fruit

explanation.surface: An approved French paper about produce asks whether it was written by a machine.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that a self-operating machine need not use modern intelligence software; the article is French, so think of un, not le.
explanation.definitionFit: An automaton is a self-operating machine or robot, the kind of device one imagines running on machine intelligence.

clue.text: Instructions regarding Cambridge University

blocks.note: re means concerning
the Massachusetts Institute of Technology is in Cambridge, Massachusetts

explanation.surface: Guidance about a famous university.
explanation.walkthrough: Cambridge here is the US city, not the English one: MIT is the Massachusetts Institute of Technology there.
explanation.definitionFit: A remit is the brief or terms of reference given to someone, setting out the task they must carry out.

clue.text: Sandbar a grave by itself, first of ships being lost

indicators.note: the first of anything is its opening member, so only the initial letter is taken
something lost has gone missing, so a letter is removed

blocks.note: a tomb is a grave
solo means alone
the opening letter

explanation.surface: A lonely grave on a sandbank marks where a ship was wrecked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sandbar' and 'ships' pull towards wreck imagery, but the grave is simply a word for the start of the answer. The lost letter comes out of a word meaning alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A tombolo is a spit or bar of sand joining an island to the mainland, a geographical term.

clue.text: New train set, handled roughly, is not lasting long

indicators.note: rough handling knocks things about, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for new
taken as written

explanation.surface: A child's new model railway, played with too roughly, will not survive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' joins the fodder as N rather than describing the toy.
explanation.definitionFit: Transient describes something brief or fleeting, existing for only a short while.

clue.text: Kept quiet and all but closed garden building

indicators.note: all but means nearly all, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: shut means closed
a shed is an outbuilding in a garden

explanation.surface: Someone kept silent about a nearly shut garden hut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'All but' reads as 'almost', describing the closing door, but here it trims a final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Being shushed means being told to be silent, so the past tense fits silenced or hushed.

clue.text: Source of medicine rapid to limit damage

indicators.note: limiting something hems it in, so one word goes round another

blocks.note: pacy means fast
harm is damage

explanation.surface: A drug delivered quickly to contain the harm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rapid' and 'limit damage' sound like emergency medicine, but pacy is a word for fast that wraps round the damage.
explanation.definitionFit: A pharmacy is a chemist's shop that dispenses drugs, so it is where patients obtain their prescriptions.

clue.text: Work appearing in youngster’s website feature

indicators.note: appearing in something means being seen inside it, so one piece is placed within another

blocks.note: op is short for opus, a work
a pup is a young animal or cheeky youngster

explanation.surface: A child's homework turns up on some feature of a website.
explanation.walkthrough: Op, short for opus, is the usual crossword word for a work.
explanation.definitionFit: A pop-up is a small window that suddenly opens over a web page, often an advertisement.

clue.text: Copper’s having volume reduced in usual approach

indicators.note: reducing something makes it shorter, so a letter is cut off

blocks.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper, plus the S
a tome is a large book

explanation.surface: A police officer turns the sound down, as is the normal practice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' and 'volume' suggest a policeman and loudness; they are the metal and a book. TOME loses its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A custom is a habitual practice or tradition, the way things are normally done.

clue.text: Follower crossing river path

indicators.note: to cross something is to span it, so one word stretches round another

blocks.note: a tail is someone who follows another
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A disciple wades across a river on a footpath.
explanation.walkthrough: TAIL takes R inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A trail is a track through countryside, a rough route for walkers.

clue.text: Increasingly upsetting most of Catholicism?

indicators.note: upsetting knocks things over and into disarray, so the letters change order

blocks.note: Rome is the seat of the Church followed by most Catholics

explanation.surface: A worried note that the Catholic Church is increasingly in turmoil.
explanation.walkthrough: Rome stands by metonymy for the Roman Catholic Church; the question mark admits this loose cryptic hint. Thomas More, the Catholic martyr, adds to the irony.
explanation.definitionFit: Used in phrases like 'more and more', the word expresses a growing degree, matching an adverb of escalation.

clue.text: Precise over author Levi

blocks.note: prim means stiffly precise and proper
O is the cricket abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: A fussy critic picks over the work of a writer.
explanation.walkthrough: An over in cricket is a set of six balls bowled from one end; scorecards abbreviate it to O.
explanation.definitionFit: Primo Levi was the Italian chemist and Holocaust survivor who wrote If This Is a Man.

clue.text: Brave figure, drunk, throttling working judge

indicators.note: throttling grips something round the throat, so one word encircles others

blocks.note: lit is slang for drunk
a machine that is on is working
to hear a case is to judge it

explanation.surface: A drunken hero strangles a judge on duty.
explanation.walkthrough: To judge a case in court is to hear it. Richard the Lionheart was the crusading English king famed for his courage.
explanation.definitionFit: A lionheart is someone of exceptional courage, likened to the boldness of a lion.

clue.text: Main tempo disrupted in theatrical performance

indicators.note: something disrupted is thrown into disorder, so its letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: The main beat of a show goes awry on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: A pantomime, or panto, is the British family stage show staged around Christmas, full of slapstick and audience participation.
explanation.definitionFit: A pantomime is a comic stage show, so it counts as one kind of dramatic entertainment.

clue.text: Rock star duly abandoning core network

indicators.note: abandoning the core throws out the middle, leaving only the ends

blocks.note: taken as written
LAN is a local area network

explanation.surface: A rock star properly quits the heart of a broadcasting network.
explanation.walkthrough: The network is a computer one, a local area network, not a TV channel.
explanation.definitionFit: Bob Dylan is the singer-songwriter who moved from folk into electric rock music in the 1960s.
